lines.vo: Writing five good things once a week did more than you'd think.
That's not cheesy. That's a ten week experiment.
So every Sunday, Tasha lists five good things in her Life Reset Planner.
Researchers split students into groups. One wrote what they were grateful for, one wrote hassles, one just wrote events.
They did it once a week, for ten weeks.
The grateful group felt better about life overall, and more hopeful about the week ahead.
They even reported about an hour and a half more exercise a week than the hassles group.
Five good things, one fresh week. That's how you stay on track.

hook: Five good things a week *lifted* their mood
